title: SBNO : Schrödinger Bridge Neural Operator for the Forward and Inverse Problems under Missing Information
claim: Our method yields uniformly lower reconstruction error than guided-diffusion and deterministic baselines across both forward and inverse problems.
layout: 2 groups of 3 error maps, left-to-right, shared colorbars
description: A single wide row of six heatmaps split into two groups. The left group is labeled Darcy Flow Forward Problem, and the right group is Navier-Stokes Backward Problem. Each group has three square error maps with titles: SBNO (ours) Error, FunDPS Error, GNOT Error. Maps use a viridis colormap, with dark purple for low error and yellow-green for high error. A colorbar sits at the right of each group, running 0 to 0.002 for Darcy and 0 to about 0.25 for Navier-Stokes. The SBNO maps are mostly dark and smooth. FunDPS shows noisy speckle on Darcy and a similar low-level pattern on Navier-Stokes. GNOT shows bright yellow-green hotspots and larger structured errors, so the contrast is visible at a glance.
caption: Reconstruction error visualization. We compare our method against FunDPS, a guided-diffusion baseline, and GNOT, a deterministic baseline. All error maps are visualized using a shared color scale for fair comparison, where lower values indicate better reconstruction accuracy.
abstract: Partial differential equation (PDE) surrogate modeling often relies on either dense observations or access to governing equations/physics constraints. In practice, observations can be sparse and partial, and the underlying physics may be partially specified or unavailable. We introduce SBNO, an equation-free paired-data diffusion bridge matching framework that learns conditional operators for both forward and inverse PDE problems under partial observations. SBNO uses diffusion SchrÃ¶dinger bridge matching to learn a pair of time-dependent drifts from a mask-aware endpoint coupling that preserves empirical input-solution pairing during training and supports both PDE-task directions within a single framework. At inference time, SBNO produces a deterministic point reconstruction by integrating the probability-flow ODE constructed from the learned drift pair, without inference-time observation or PDE guidance-weight tuning. On five PDE benchmarks with 5% observations, SBNO achieves superior or comparable accuracy to baselines while demonstrating lower test-instance error dispersion. Furthermore, SBNO is at least $9.7 \times$ faster and reduces GPU memory by at least $4.3 \times$ compared to guided-diffusion baselines.
